1
A cyclist has a speed of 5 m s–1 and a small car has a speed of 12 m s–1.
Which statement does not give a reasonable estimate?
J.
A
The kinetic energy of the cyclist is 1 × 103
J.
B
The kinetic energy of the car is 7 × 104
kg m s–1.
C
The momentum of the cyclist is 4 × 102
D
The momentum of the car is 2 × 105
kg m s–1.

hints: Start by estimating sensible masses: about $70$-$90 \text{ kg}$ for cyclist plus bike and about $1000 \text{ kg}$ for a small car.
Recall the governing relations $p = mv$ in $\text{kg m s}^{-1}$ and $E_k = \frac{1}{2}mv^2$ in $\text{J}$ using $5 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $12 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Calculate each $p$ and $E_k$ to order of magnitude and look for the value that is more than ten times too large.
walkthrough: Assume reasonable masses: $m \approx 80 \text{ kg}$ for cyclist plus bicycle and $m \approx 1000 \text{ kg}$ for a small car.
For the cyclist, momentum $p = mv \approx 80 \times 5 = 400 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$, so $4 \times 10^2 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$ is reasonable.
For the cyclist, kinetic energy $E_k = \frac{1}{2}mv^2 \approx 0.5 \times 80 \times 5^2 = 1000 \text{ J}$, so $1 \times 10^3 \text{ J}$ is reasonable.
For the car, kinetic energy $E_k = \frac{1}{2}mv^2 \approx 0.5 \times 1000 \times 12^2 = 72000 \text{ J}$, so $7 \times 10^4 \text{ J}$ is reasonable.

For the car, momentum $p = mv \approx 1000 \times 12 = 1.2 \times 10^4 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$, which is about ten times smaller than $2 \times 10^5 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$ and would need a lorry-like mass. This is option D.

A.explanation: Reasonable. With total mass about $80 \text{ kg}$ at $5 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, $E_k = \frac{1}{2}mv^2$ is about $1 \times 10^3 \text{ J}$.

B.explanation: Reasonable. With car mass about $1000 \text{ kg}$ at $12 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, $E_k = \frac{1}{2}mv^2$ is about $7 \times 10^4 \text{ J}$.

C.explanation: Reasonable. With total mass about $80 \text{ kg}$ at $5 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, $p = mv$ is about $4 \times 10^2 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$.

D.explanation: Not reasonable. With car mass about $1000 \text{ kg}$ at $12 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, $p = mv$ is about $1 \times 10^4 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$, far smaller than $2 \times 10^5 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$.
